transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (CTO - BrightRetail), Ethan Cole (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (PM)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on Redwood's hosted self-serve API for a PLG quickstart; customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for initial feature, wants fast time-to-first-token and clear path to Dedicated if needed; security and data residency questions; agreed next steps around pricing, security docs, and a pilot benchmark.

Topics: quickstart / free credits; time-to-first-token; performance expectations; dedicated vs private tradeoffs; SOC2/KMS/SSO; rollout timeline and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off  i'm samir, account exec for redwood inference, with laura our solutions engineer. can you do quick intros?
[00:15] Maya (BrightRetail): sure, i'm maya, cto at brightretail, we build a personalized emails and search feature. we're exploring LLMs to power search-rewrite and product descriptions.
[00:28] Priya (BrightRetail): priya here, product, i'm owner for the search initiative. timeline is tight  want to ship an mvp in 6-8 weeks.
[00:35] Ethan (BrightRetail): ethan, ml eng, i'll run experiments and care about latency and cost.
[00:40] Laura (Redwood): great, thanks. quick agenda: quickstart experience, free credits/time-to-first-token, hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), security, and next steps.
[01:05] Samir: to frame  many teams start with our hosted api via self-serve, get credits, and have predictable first-token times. then if needed they move to dedicated or private. curious what your success criteria look like?
[01:22] Maya: low friction onboarding is key  ideally get a token within an hour, run some experiments same day. second is production constraints: p95 latency under 300ms for short completions and cost under $X per 1k tokens  we'll define numbers later.
[01:40] Ethan: also data controls  we can't send PII to a third-party in some cases, so we need clarity on data retention and optional VPC/private deployment.
[01:55] Laura: totally  hosted is easiest for quickstart, Dedicated gives reserved capacity and SLAs, and Private gives VPC/on-prem for data residency. we can map your constraints to those.
[02:20] Maya: what's the actual step to get started? free credits? sdk?
[02:28] Samir: you can sign up self-serve, we give trial credits. typical time-to-first-token is 10-30 minutes if you follow quickstart; sometimes folks hit 1-2 hours with network/permission snags. laura will share the quickstart checklist.
[02:45] Laura: the quickstart is one page  api key, install sdk or curl, run a sample generate, and you'll see tokens. i'll drop the quickstart link and a sample notebook.
[03:05] Priya: great  do you have code samples in ts and python?
[03:10] Laura: yes, both  we'll include typescript node and python examples plus a notebook that shows embeddings and simple reranking.
[03:28] Ethan: latency  when you say 300ms p95, is that for hosted? or dedicated?
[03:35] Laura: hosted p95 depends on model and sequence length; for small models we see sub-200ms in many regions for short sequences, but higher for bigger models. Dedicated can give more predictable latency because it's reserved GPU pools; and Private with co-located infra can be lowest-latency but requires more setup.
[04:05] Maya: ok, we initially want hosted to move fast, then dedicated if traffic grows. question about kv cache and batching  how much do we need to think about those?
[04:20] Laura: good question. our runtime does automatic prefix KV cache and continuous batching. you can tune batching policies but quickstart is typically fine out of the box. note: docs sometimes say KV cash  yeah transcriber sometimes mis-hears that.
[04:45] Ethan: helpful. what about quantization and model variants  can we try smaller quantized variants for cost savings?
[04:55] Laura: yes, we surface quantization guidance and recommended model variants per workload. the platform will also suggest batching and quantization settings based on token distribution.
[05:15] Maya: security  do you have SOC2, SSO, KMS? how do we keep logs/audits?
[05:25] Samir: we are SOC2 compliant, we support SAML/SSO and RBAC. for keys you can bring your own KMS/HSM in private deployments; hosted supports encrypted at rest and customer-managed keys for higher tiers. we also keep audit logs with per-request metadata in the console.
[05:50] Priya: any concerns about multi-tenancy on hosted?
[05:55] Laura: hosted is multi-tenant but we offer isolated Dedicated pools for customers that need it. for strict compliance we recommend Private.
[06:10] Ethan: does hosted persist data by default? what's the retention policy?
[06:15] Samir: by default request logging is retained for X days (we'll attach exact policy), and you can opt-out or configure retention; enterprise customers can set retention via console or choose Private where no requests leave your VPC.
[06:35] Maya: trial credits  how much do you usually provide?
[06:40] Samir: trial credits vary; we'll give enough to prototype and run a small benchmark (we typically do a few hundred dollars equivalent). for pilot engagements we can expand credits based on defined scope.
[07:00] Priya: ok good. on timeline  if we start today how fast to run a pilot?
[07:05] Laura: quickstart can be same day for dev, but for pilot benchmark we usually schedule a run with an SE to ensure instrumentation; we can do that within a week after credits and sample data are provided.
[07:25] Ethan: benchmark  we want to compare latency/cost across smaller models on hosted and a dedicated configuration. can we run a side-by-side?
[07:35] Laura: yes, we can run hosted traffic and replicate on a dedicated pool or a private instance. SE will script the workload.
[07:48] Maya: procurement  if we move to dedicated what's procurement like? legal?
[07:55] Samir: for Dedicated we do a reserved capacity contract, usually monthly or annual commit. procurement typically asks for SOC2, DPA, and standard terms  we have enterprise contracts and templates we can share.
[08:15] Priya: any major gotchas? network config, vpc peering?
[08:22] Laura: for Private or VPC you need some network setup (VPC peering, firewall rules). we provide a runbook. sometimes infra teams misconfigure subnets and it delays by a day.
[08:38] Ethan: do you have examples of customers that started self-serve and then moved to dedicated?
[08:44] Samir: yes  several SaaS customers; they'll ramp on hosted, then when usage and latency needs grow they purchase dedicated and we assist with migration.
[09:00] Maya: specifics  we are 6-8 week mvp. success = feature launched to 10k users, 95th pct latency under 300ms, cost target TBD.
[09:15] Samir: makes sense. is data residency a hard requirement or just preference?
[09:20] Maya: preference for now, but some catalogs may require stricter residency later.
[09:28] Laura: we have region selection for hosted and dedicated, and private for strict residency.
[09:40] Ethan: what about SDK integration  favourite approach? wrapper vs direct api?
[09:48] Laura: many teams use our SDK for retry and streaming but you can call the REST endpoint directly. SDK includes helper for streaming and function/tool calling.
[10:05] Priya: billing visibility  can we see token-level breakdown?
[10:10] Samir: yes, console provides token-level cost/latency breakdown per route and per model. you can also export reports.
[10:22] Maya: sample notebook and quickstart please.
[10:28] Laura: will send  includes node/python snippets and an embedding + rerank notebook.
[10:40] Ethan: regarding evaluation  we want to run our prompts through a small eval harness. do you have built-in eval tooling?
[10:48] Laura: we have Redwood Optimize tooling recommendations and eval hooks; for pilots SEs often run evals with customers and set regression alerts.
[11:05] Samir: any competitors you're currently looking at?
[11:10] Maya: openai and anthropic mainly; also evaluating on-prem runtimes like triton.
[11:18] Laura: that's common  we focus on production economics and migration path across hosted/dedicated/private.
[11:35] Ethan: technical question  can we pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts?
[11:42] Laura: yes, you can pin versions and do canary/A-B and automatic fallback policies. console supports rollouts and tracing.
[12:00] Priya: ok good. security review  laura, can you share SOC2 cert and DPA?
[12:06] Laura: yes, i'll share SOC2, DPA, SSO guide, and KMS docs. note that for private we can also support customer-managed HSM.
[12:20] Maya: any rough pricing for hosted to estimate costs?
[12:25] Samir: i'll send a pricing range but rough ballpark depends on model size and tokens. for embeddings and small gen models cost-per-1k tokens is lower; we'll provide an estimate for your expected traffic.
[12:40] Ethan: about the pilot benchmark  what metrics do you recommend we gather?
[12:45] Laura: latency p50/p95, tokens-per-second throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and error rates. also measure cold-starts and KV cache hit-rate for long sessions.
[13:00] Maya: ok we'll prepare sample payloads and expected concurrency.
[13:10] Samir: perfect. anything else on hosted vs dedicated migration path?
[13:18] Laura: migration is straightforward  same API, pin versions and then switch routing to dedicated pool. SE helps with load testing. sometimes you need minor config changes for quantization or batching.
[13:35] Ethan: can we get a sandbox dedicated pool for the benchmark or do we run on hosted?
[13:42] Laura: we can provision a small dedicated pool for pilot but that typically requires a short contract; alternatively we replicate on hosted with dedicated-like settings to approximate.
[13:58] Maya: procurement will want to see a contract sample and DPA.
[14:05] Samir: will include those in the doc pack.
[14:12] Priya: any known limits on rate-limits or token caps during trial?
[14:18] Samir: trials have soft limits we can raise for pilot runs on request  we'll coordinate with infra.
[14:30] Ethan: for telemetry  can we push traces to our observability stack?
[14:35] Laura: yes, we have tracing hooks and can export logs; console shows per-route dashboards.
[14:50] Maya: noted. okay let's talk concrete next steps  who owns what?
[14:58] Samir: i'll send pricing + quickstart guide. laura will share security pack. ethan will send sample payloads. we'll schedule a pilot benchmark next week if possible.
[15:12] Priya: timeline: we'll aim to be ready for a pilot by week of 3/30.
[15:20] Laura: i'll propose specific slots.
[15:28] Samir: awesome. last question  are there any hidden costs for streaming or function calls?
[15:35] Laura: streaming counts tokens as normal; function/tool calling is supported and billed on tokens and any additional model calls. no hidden infra fees beyond dedicated contract commitment.
[15:50] Ethan: one more: error handling patterns for rate limits?
[15:55] Laura: SDK has backoff/retry and idempotency recommendations; we can share best practices.
[16:10] Maya: okay thanks, this is helpful.
[16:15] Samir: thanks all  we'll follow up with the doc pack and proposed pilot slots.
[16:25] Priya: appreciate it.
[16:30] Maya: bye.

(Transcript cut off; meeting duration 42 minutes  remaining time included Q/A and wrap-up.)
